**Indikator** (Indicator) refers to the quantitative metrics used to measure and evaluate the quality of atrial fibrillation treatment within the Danish healthcare system. As a core component of the quality development framework detailed in the 2024 AFDK (Atrieflimren i Danmark) report, these indicators are essential for ensuring uniform, evidence-based, and patient-centered care for a frequent and potentially serious chronic heart condition [^src1]. 

A central decision documented in the report is the retention of a specific indicator, with its quality standard officially set at [[50-percent|50-percent]] [^src1]. This established threshold directly impacts clinical practice and the ongoing evaluation of treatment quality across the national database [^src1]. By maintaining this standard, the AFDK steering group aims to track clinical practices effectively, even while acknowledging methodological limitations in data collection, to continuously improve patient outcomes [^src1].
